Bug_Details:
Explicitly calling Thread.run() method will execute in the caller's thread of control.  Instead, call Thread.start() for the intended behavior.
Examples:
Thread t = new Thread();
t.run();            // use t.start() instead
new Thread().run(); // same violation
Bug_Explanation: Explicitly calling Thread.run() method will execute in the caller's thread of control. Instead, call Thread.start() for the intended behavior.
Trigger_Explanation: The JUNIT test case calls the `showBug` method of the DontCallThreadRun class. This method contains two Thread objects, one directly and one indirectly (through anonymous inner class), that are created and started using `run` method, thereby triggering the bug.
